readout_other: verbal report of tactile, temperature and pain sensation thresholds.
direction_notes: Focused ultrasound evoked tactile, thermal (warmth or cold, depending on ambient water temperature) and pain sensations by activating cutaneous and deep (soft tissue, bone, joint) receptor structures in the hand; thresholds rose moving from fingers to forearm and with deeper placement of the focal region.

exposures.label: Focused ultrasound to skin/deep receptor structures of the hand (480 kHz)

target.label: skin, soft tissue, bone and joints of the hand (fingers, palm, forearm)

timing.protocol_description: The focusing irradiator and the subject's hand were submerged in a water bath (30, 35 or 40C); stimuli of a given duration were applied at irregular intervals with intensity rising from stimulus to stimulus, first for 1 msec, then 10 and 100 msec, until tactile, then temperature, then pain sensations appeared. The focal region could be moved from the skin surface into deeper soft tissue, bone or joint using a coordinate positioning device.

exposures.label: Focused ultrasound to thermode-defined warm/cold skin spots (1.95 MHz, one of three frequencies compared)

target.label: skin, soft tissue, bone and joints of the hand (fingers, palm, forearm)

timing.protocol_description: At room temperature (21-23C) a warm or cold thermode (tip diameter about 1 mm) was used to locate 'warm' and 'cold' spots on the palm skin; these same spots were then stimulated with focused ultrasound (0.887, 1.95 and 2.67 MHz; 1 and 10 msec duration; water temperature 34-36C), and the resulting cold or warmth sensation was independent of whether the spot had been classed as warm or cold by the thermode.
